response.sql: WITH type_avg AS (SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price FROM Products GROUP BY production_type_code HAVING AVG(unit_price) IS NOT NULL), base AS (SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS baseline FROM Products), kept AS (SELECT t.production_type_code, t.avg_price FROM type_avg t JOIN base b ON b.baseline IS NOT NULL WHERE t.avg_price > b.baseline), kept_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS m FROM kept), final AS (SELECT k.avg_price FROM kept k JOIN kept_mean km ON k.avg_price > km.m) SELECT AVG(f.avg_price) AS avg_type_average_price, AVG(f.avg_price - b.baseline) AS avg_above_baseline, AVG(f.avg_price - km.m) AS avg_above_kept_mean FROM final f CROSS JOIN base b CROSS JOIN kept_mean km;

assumptions.assumption: Types whose unit_price values are all NULL have no average and are excluded from the type averages.
If no types remain after both filters, the query returns one row of NULLs rather than zero rows.
